articles.title: Paying $1,000 to get past the process
A default risk before the trial

personal_account.status: Attributed recollection; individual case documents not supplied
personal_account.lender_description: Rigler thinks the lender was a micro-lender; identity unconfirmed
reported_sequence: Sued over a debt in what he describes as the lowest court
Directed to a pretrial session involving someone he understood to be a court-appointed mediator
Repeatedly said he did not want mediation
Understood nonappearance could lead to default and could not obtain an opt-out while unrepresented
Appeared in person to decline and told the judge he was there under duress
Recalls that the case then went away
reported_concerns: Feared supplying facts to establish the claimant's case
Believed counsel could avoid his personal appearance
Interpreted the added appearance as an opportunity to obtain default before trial
unknowns: Case date, court, precinct, and docket
Lender and law firm identities and claimed amount
Answer, notices, mediation referral, objections, and rulings
Exact statements and whether any session was governed by mediation confidentiality
Any distinction between represented and unrepresented parties
Lawyer work, any separate debt payment, and final disposition
personal_account.evidence_location: Relevant private Daisy case; no case path supplied

research_limitations: JP1 is a published comparison, not an identified court in the recollection
Current rules do not establish historical governing rules without a case date
No general exemption from personal attendance based solely on having counsel is established
No finding of manufactured defaults, debt validity, sanction legality, or judicial misconduct
